summary: Gustav Haloun specialized in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna, Leipzig under August Conrady, and Prague. He later served as Director at Göttingen (1931–1938) and held the Chair of Chinese at Cambridge (1938–1951).

Gustav Herbig was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig and earned his Ph.D. and habilitation at the University of Munich. He served as a librarian at the Bavarian State Library and as professor at Rostock, Breslau, and Munich.

Gustav Mensching worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Göttingen, Berlin, Marburg under Rudolf Otto and Friedrich Heiler, and Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel. He held professorships at the University of Latvia and Kiel, followed by posts at Bonn.

Linguist Gustav Meyer earned his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau, where he studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He taught at Charles University and served as associate professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at the University of Graz from 1877 to 1897.

Gustav Roth worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle-Wittenberg, Munich under Helmut Hoffmann, and Patna University under several traditional and academic teachers, he served at the University of Göttingen (1965–1981) and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Gustav Salomon Oppert was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bonn, Berlin, and Halle (PhD). He served at the Bodleian Library, Presidency University as Professor of Sanskrit (1872–1894), and later taught at Humboldt University of Berlin.

Gustave Liétard worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the Collège de Toul and earned his Dr.med. at the University of Strasbourg, studying under Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann and Philippe Édouard Foucaux.
Gustavo Benavides is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who held an attested post at Villanova University in 1995 and 2004.

Gustavo Moura works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his BA at the University of Chester (2013–2016), his master's at the Federal University of Paraíba (2015–2017), and his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University (2018–2022).

Gustaw Blatt was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jagiellonian University under Lucjan Malinowski and at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, Ernst Windisch, and August Leskien. He taught at the Jewish Gymnasium in Brody and became a professor at Lviv.
Guus Kroonen is a linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky. He has held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen around 2013 and at Leiden University in 2016.

Guy Bugault worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, studying under Olivier Lacombe. He held teaching posts at Paris Nanterre University and served as Professor of Indian and Comparative Philosophy at Paris-Sorbonne University from circa 1968 to 1985.

Guy G. Stroumsa is a religious studies scholar who studied at Paris, Hebrew University, EPHE, and Harvard. He was an associate professor at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and later served as Professor of the Study of the Abrahamic Religions at Oxford.

Guy Newland is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia and with traditional Tibetan teachers, later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University.
Guybon Henry Damant worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, from 1864 to 1868 under John Peile and Edward Byles Cowell, earning an M.A.
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Gyatsho Tshering was a Tibetology scholar educated at the University of Calcutta. He co-founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, serving as its acting director in 1972 and director from 1974 to 1998.

Gyoei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Daigakurin. He served as a lecturer at Toyo University, professor at the University of Tokyo in 1928, and president of Taisho University around 1940 to 1943.

Gyoei Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Rissho University as assistant professor and professor, and served as a staff member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Gyoko Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He later served there as assistant professor, professor, and professor emeritus, and was a former specially appointed professor at Minobusan University.
